status: branch prepared from pushed commit; implementation is next after report review
scope: Gemma4 multimodal prefix attention support in opt-in ROCM_SEGMENTED_ATTN
observations: Segmented backend currently advertises supports_mm_prefix=False. Its ROCm metadata builder does not copy CommonAttentionMetadata.mm_req_doc_ranges.

Existing Triton builder uses compute_mm_prefix_range_tensor; its metadata provides both CPU ranges and a device tensor. Segmented backend needs equivalent metadata propagation and unified-fallback forwarding.
Triton attention helpers use inclusive start/end and start<end validity. Query and key must belong to the same range to gain bidirectional visibility.

Gemma4 sets mm_prefix_clamp_sliding_window for sliding layers: range visibility is intersected with the past bound (query-key)<window. Future keys within the same image range are allowed; do not impose a symmetric future-window bound.

Segmented stage currently prunes key range_end at the causal query-tile end. Native multimodal masking must also extend traversal to visible future keys; changing only the per-score mask would still omit them.

Text/decode behavior and no-range specializations should remain unchanged. Preserve supported features, typed config selection, cache semantics and the cache-only MTP path. New kernel fingerprints/caches must remain separate from this frozen serving study.
validation_plan: Compare native multimodal attention against dense FP32 masks and existing unified Triton across local/global D256/512, GQA2/8, FP8/BF16 KV, variable query lengths, multiple/empty ranges and range/page/tile boundaries.
Cover chunked prefill and long-query unified fallback, decode, MTP shared target-cache readers, graph capture/replay and KV cache immutability.
Validate true multimodal Gemma model loading/serving on TP2 with an image prompt after numerical tests pass; these completed benchmarks are language-model-only.
